reason: Throughout this passage, the Hebrew people openly and repeatedly express their views, complaints, and concerns. They murmur against Moses multiple times (וַיִּלֹּנוּ הָעָם עַל־ מֹשֶׁה), ask questions about their conditions (מַה־ נִּשְׁתֶּה - 'what shall we drink?'), and directly argue with Moses about food and water (וַיָּ֤רֶב הָעָ֛ם עִם־ מֹשֶׁ֔ה). There are no laws or rules preventing them from speaking, and their complaints are heard and often addressed by Moses and God. While Moses occasionally encourages faith or discourages fear (אַל־ תִּירָאוּ), this represents selective guidance on attitude rather than a systematic discouragement of expression itself.
